slides.text: Pick the **shape** before you write the words.
slides.sub: A statement is one sentence that earns the whole slide. Keep the sub short and it carries the claim.

columns.b: Set two or three peers side by side so the reader scans the difference fast.
Bucket related ideas under short headers instead of one long paragraph.
Give each idea equal weight when no single one should win the slide.

slides.heading: Panel reads like a status board
slides.sub: Use it for rows of named items with a value and a state dot. Header and footer are optional.

slides.heading: Chips for a quick taxonomy
slides.sub: Drop a row of short labels when the point is breadth, not depth.
slides.mono: one accent, sentence case, no shouting

slides.label: slide types in one design system

slides.heading: Timeline walks a process
slides.sub: Five steps fit cleanly. More than that and the labels start to crowd the edges.

fixed layout keeps the eye moving in a square
value type so the number reads from the back row
accent hue across every card on the slide

slides.heading: Receipt makes a claim auditable
slides.sub: Use it when the slide needs evidence fields, not prose. Up to six rows plus a stamp.

slides.text: Write the slide the reader **already wishes** they had.
slides.author: Atris deck engine

slides.headline: Hero centers one **big idea**
slides.sub: Reach for it when the slide is a moment, not a table. Everything centers under one rule.
Interstitial is a chapter card. Big type, lots of air, a kicker to mark the turn.

slides.headline: Lede opens like a feature story
slides.dek: A magazine intro slide: one strong headline, a deck of supporting text, and a byline that grounds it.

slides.heading: Prose is for paragraphs
paragraphs: When the content is genuinely a few sentences of argument, do not force it into cards. Prose gives the reader room to follow a line of thought without a widget in the way.
The engine fits one font size across every paragraph and floats them down to the slide floor, so two or three short paragraphs stay readable and balanced.

slides.heading: Split pairs text with one figure
slides.body: Put the explanation on the left and let a single number or short phrase carry the right side. It reads as claim plus proof without a full panel.
slides.accentSub: of the slide is text; the accent is the punchline the reader remembers.

slides.heading: Bullets, done with restraint

items.text: Keep it to seven or fewer
items.sub: the engine shrinks type as the list grows

items.text: Lead each item with a verb or a noun
Add a sub only when it earns its line
Prefer a real list over a wall of cards

slides.sub: A true bullet list: accent dot, text, no card around each line.
